source.title: AlphaZeroBeta: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Market-Neutral Portfolios
source.author: Boris Belyakov

thesis: A recurrent policy with explicit dollar-neutral projection, a rolling benchmark-correlation penalty, and a turnover penalty can improve risk-adjusted out-of-sample returns while preserving near-zero benchmark correlation compared with an otherwise identical return-seeking recurrent policy without the correlation penalty.
mechanism: Center each target weight vector so sum(weights)=0 and scale it to gross exposure <= 1.
Optimize risk-adjusted benchmark-relative return with a rolling correlation penalty (lambda_corr=0.5).
Use a CNN-GRU policy/value network and recurrent PPO with gamma=0.99, GAE=0.95, clip=0.20, learning_rate=3e-4, 10 PPO epochs, and a 100-observation multi-scale window.

validation_contract.split: 36-month train + 6-month validation + non-overlapping 6-month test; advance 6 months; reset model weights each fold
validation_contract.primary_comparator: same architecture, data, seed set, split, and costs with lambda_corr=0

primary_cost_assumption.classification: pre-registered sensitivity assumption, not realized execution cost

confirmation_gate: Across the aggregated untouched test folds, absolute benchmark correlation is <= 0.15 under the primary cost assumption.
After-cost annualized Sharpe is greater than the lambda_corr=0 ablation on the same test observations.
Absolute benchmark correlation is lower than the lambda_corr=0 ablation on the same test observations.
Dollar-neutrality is mechanically satisfied: max absolute net exposure <= 1e-6 and gross exposure <= 1 plus numerical tolerance.
No split, universe cutoff, feature definition, cost assumption, or gate is changed after inspecting test outcomes without a new hypothesis version.
falsifiers: The confirmatory OOS folds do not satisfy the correlation gate.
The explicit correlation penalty does not improve both benchmark correlation and Sharpe versus lambda_corr=0 on the same OOS observations.
The result depends on future constituent membership, backward-filled information, or test-period data used in universe selection or normalization.
The strategy loses its positive risk-adjusted result under the pre-registered primary cost assumption.
The result cannot be reproduced from frozen dataset and weight artifacts.

replication_boundary.reason: The paper uses licensed Bloomberg and Financial Modeling Prep data and states that the complete code base is not redistributable.
replication_boundary.aaarts_target: Independent mechanism replication on a frozen locally available market dataset. Exact paper performance is not claimed.
replication_boundary.survivorship_requirement: A confirmatory run requires point-in-time constituent membership or an explicitly bounded fixed-universe caveat; otherwise the run remains feasibility-only.

cpu_side: dataset normalization and PIT-safe feature construction
gpu_only: recurrent PPO parameter optimization for a bounded fold/seed run
